\begin{lemma}[Gaussian stability at zero correlation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianHalfspaceStability_zero}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianHalfspaceStability_zero}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianHalfspaceStability, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF_quantile, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianQuantile}
\difficulty{4}
For every $\alpha\in[0,1]$, the Gaussian halfspace stability with correlation parameter
$0$ and measure parameter $\alpha$ equals $\alpha^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian stability at correlation one]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianHalfspaceStability_one}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianHalfspaceStability_one}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianHalfspaceStability, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianCDF_quantile, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianQuantile}
\difficulty{4}
For every $\alpha\in[0,1]$, the Gaussian halfspace stability with correlation parameter
$1$ and measure parameter $\alpha$ equals $\alpha$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Half-measure Gaussian stability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianHalfspaceStability_half}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianHalfspaceStability_half}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianHalfspaceStability, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.standardGaussianCDF_zero, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.gaussianQuadrantProbability, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianQuantile_eq}
\difficulty{3}
For every real $\rho$, the Gaussian halfspace stability at measure parameter $1/2$
equals the probability that two independent standard real Gaussians $G,H$ satisfy
$G\le0$ and $\rho G+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,H\le0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Gaussian rotation sensitivity bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_borell}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_borell}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.borell, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianHalfspaceStability, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianHalfspaceStability_one, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianHalfspaceStability_zero, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_eq_stability, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_pi_div_two, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable. For every
$\theta\in[0,\pi/2]$, $$2\bigl(\gamma_n(A)-H(\cos\theta,\gamma_n(A))\bigr)\le
s_A(\theta),$$ where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure, $s_A(\theta)$ is the
probability that membership changes under $g\mapsto\cos(\theta)g+\sin(\theta)h$ for
independent standard Gaussian vectors $g,h$, and $H(\rho,\alpha)$ is the Gaussian
halfspace stability defined using threshold $\Phi^{-1}(\alpha)$ for $0<\alpha<1$, with
values $0$ for $\alpha\le0$ and $1$ for $\alpha\ge1$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable with standard
Gaussian measure $1/2$. For every $\theta\in[0,\pi/2]$, its Gaussian rotation
sensitivity, the probability that membership in $A$ changes under the rotation
$g\mapsto\cos(\theta)g+\sin(\theta)h$ for independent standard Gaussian vectors $g,h$,
satisfies $$\frac{\theta}{\pi}\le s_A(\theta).$$
\end{theorem}
